mentions.name: Hyperclay
mentions.description: This platform lets developers build advanced software in a single HTML file by storing state in the document itself, with host-granted APIs to sync changes with live collaborators, extract data via a simple JSON map config, and boot a full content CMS from the same config. It includes a hosted platform and source-available native offline apps, with about a dozen paying users and a long-term vision of the file type being supported by other companies' tools and hosting.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on a way to make some pretty advanced software in a single HTML file.

The idea is simple: store state you'd normally store in a separate database in the document itself.

Then, also give the the document a bunch of powerful APIs granted to it by its host:

(1) Sync changes to the document with live collaborators

(2) Extract data from the document using a simple JSON map config

(3) Boot up a full content CMS from the same simple JSON map config

mentions.name: Hyperclay
mentions.description: Hyperclay packages HTML files as portable, editable apps that contain their own editable UI. These simple apps can be used for planning, editing emails, writing blog posts, and more; they can be edited locally on a Mac and sync live to the web, letting users design their own document format on the fly and display it however they want.
